headline_verdict: M145 arithmetic, identity, and claim hygiene pass. Its numbers are conservative only for an explicitly one-cycle, always-ready synthetic control recurrence; they are not a finite upper bound on general M144 ready/valid execution and are not cycle-exact engine, physical, or system results.

findings.title: A minimum endpoint floor cannot establish a finite execution upper bound
findings.evidence: M145 charges one cycle for 1332 zero-PWP and 300 zero-correction units, but both the M144 contract and SVA describe a minimum one-cycle endpoint, not a maximum. The sealed M144 TB legally uses PWP countdown 2+sequence[0] and correction countdown 3+sequence[0], already demonstrating allowed response delays beyond one cycle.
findings.impact: The 135739441-cycle B4 value is not an upper bound on the sealed M144 environment or on a future engine; it is only the result of defining zero-work service as exactly one charged cycle.
findings.required_fix: Freeze exact zero-work bypass latency or a proven maximum endpoint response bound, then replay it in the cycle recurrence. Rename the current result to a one-cycle endpoint sensitivity until that contract exists.

findings.title: Always-ready and bounded-ack assumptions are missing from the upper-bound claim
findings.evidence: M144 exposes descriptor_ready, pwp_ready, correction_ready and external outer_commit_done_valid with no finite latency bound. M145 charges accepted control edges but no waiting time. Arbitrary legal backpressure makes completion time unbounded, and the five-job VCS run does not bind heldout response latency.
findings.impact: Serial addition proves an upper bound only over an invented always-ready control recurrence, not over general M144 ready/valid behavior.
findings.required_fix: State always-ready/exact-one-cycle assumptions in contract, result status and paper-safe text, or add bounded-liveness assumptions and a cycle-exact 69120-unit replay.

findings.title: Several serial charges may duplicate boundaries already present in M143r2
findings.evidence: M143r2 already contains one descriptor-fill boundary per unit, one controller dispatch edge per unit, 160 accumulator flush edges and 480000 commit cycles. Its recurrence source explicitly uses producer_tokens+1 and dispatch+1.
findings.impact: Duplication is safe for a conditional upper bound, but the 278432 cycles cannot be interpreted as measured M144 overhead or a clean per-edge delta.
findings.required_fix: Build an edge-labeled before/after recurrence and mark each existing, replaced and newly inserted edge exactly once.

findings.title: M144 VCS coverage is structural, not heldout cycle evidence
findings.evidence: The sealed run covers five one-row jobs, eight descriptors and one barrier, versus 69120 units and 160 barriers in M145.
findings.impact: It validates protocol mechanisms but not the charged heldout schedule or B4 cycle bound.
findings.required_fix: Drive an abstracted 69120-unit service trace through M144 or a differential RTL cycle simulator with exact endpoint latencies.

findings.title: The area delta is a flattened integrated-netlist difference
findings.evidence: 3902.472014 minus 2562.462012 equals 1340.010002 um2, and the 286 sequential-cell delta exactly reconciles the 286 wrapper architectural state bits. Both designs were separately flattened and optimized.
findings.impact: The differential is trustworthy as same-flow integrated area change, but not as a separately isolated wrapper block area.
findings.required_fix: Label it integrated flattened delta; preserve hierarchy or use matched incremental synthesis if standalone wrapper area is needed.

findings.title: Timing is technically met with only 1.9 ps reported setup margin
findings.evidence: M144 reports +0.0019 ns setup at 3 ns, only 0.0633% of the period, and 0.0000 ns rounded hold. The critical endpoint is correction_accept under ideal clock, ZeroWireload, and zero macros.
findings.impact: Minor macro/wiring/clock effects can erase the margin; this is logic-only admission, not physical frequency evidence.
findings.required_fix: Add margin or pipeline the correction-accept cone, then run macro-inclusive PT with propagated clocks and wiring.

findings.title: B2/B3 bounds have no matching M144 RTL geometry
findings.evidence: M144 production fatals unless BANKS=4, while M145 reports B2 and B3 charged bounds by adding the same scalar charge.
findings.impact: B2/B3 are analytical sensitivities and can be mistaken for implemented points.
findings.required_fix: Mark B2/B3 model-only or implement and verify matched M144 configurations.
